BenLstmBidder reads BEN's own bidding nets: output layer under layers/time_distributed/layer as well as layers/dense

E9-25's first box run failed loading BEN's GIB-BBO-8742 net (KeyError layers/dense/vars/0). BEN's TF2 bidders have
the house bidders' architecture and settings (193 inputs, three 256-unit LSTMs, batch-norm epsilon 0.001, a 40-way
softmax Dense) but wrap the Dense in TimeDistributed, which Keras saves under another path. The loader now takes
either path and names the file when it finds neither. House bidders load as before (layers/dense comes first).

Checked with BEN's file fetched from its public repository (SHA-256 b0dff3df..., the pinned one; not stored here):
on 2,000 random deals BEN's net opens 1NT only on 15 to 17 points, passes as dealer only with 11 or fewer, and opens
as the house bidder does on 99.2% of deals; E9-25's study ran on 3 positions with the BEN replay. Test with
synthetic weights in both layouts; the bidder tests (56 passed, 5 skipped) pass.

DDS position cache: BRIDGE_DDS_CACHE_SYNC=NORMAL lowers SQLite's sync level for one run (default FULL)

For Gen X Stu's run on azure4, which shares one Premium P10 disk with the Gen 9 cohort. At 01:33 UTC the box
showed 25-41% CPU idle, 4-17% iowait and 598 writes/s at 17 ms, with 166 flushes/s. Most of the writes are
the cohort's DDS-cache inserts, synced FULL. With WAL, NORMAL syncs at checkpoints only: a power loss can drop
the last entries, which are then solved again, and the file is never corrupted. Cards and results do not
change. Unset, the cache syncs FULL as before. Any other value is refused.

tests/test_dds_cache_sync.py: FULL by default, NORMAL when asked, OFF refused. tests/test_dds_cache.py passes.
